items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: Estevez is mentioned only as the name of the movie 'Another Stakeout' (Emilio Estevez) for which the interviewee played a session; no personal interaction or relationship is described.

ctx.x: Well you already started to answer a question that this led to, and you sound like a fairly modest guy but can you tell us why you were chosen so many times over the years for the work you do?

Good question. You know nobody gets thrown into this business and starts doing all the work right away. It’s a slow burn usually. And somebody, maybe somebody hears you play and you get an opportunity, you know, somebody hires you. “Hey I heard this saxophone player” whatever, “at this club. I wonder if they’d be right for this recording session. Does anybody know this person?” And people ask. And you go, “Oh yeah, that’s Bob Shepherd, oh yeah, of course we know Bob Shepherd, he’s great.” You know. And then you…

Estevez, but it was a hundred piece orchestra and I got called to do this thing. And it was on recommendations from some colleagues I’d been playing in a couple of kicks bands with. Warren Luening, a really great trumpet player from here who’s passed away, and George Graham, who played lead trumpet with many big bands here. Both mentors of mine. And the contractor had gone through the list of players and there was a lot of work happening that week and they go, “Well try this guy, Wayne, you know, I play in Bob…
